title: Whack-a-mole
briefing: A spam script forked itself. Three copies are hammering the mail queue.
Killing them one PID at a time is a losing game.
tips: `pkill NAME` kills every process whose command matches NAME, all at once.
objective: Kill all the spam-blast processes (there are several).
hints: They all share a name. There's a command that kills by name, not PID.
`pkill` matches every process by command. `pgrep spam-blast` shows how many there are.
explanation: `pkill NAME` signals every matching process in one shot, and `pgrep NAME` lists them without killing. When a program spawns many copies, killing by name beats chasing PIDs.
